text:
maya.dev: fyi, AkmeCorp is on us — hitting p99 spikes to ~5s during their nightly billing window. Support escalated. Looks like Dedicated pool for their priority queue is thrashing warmups / attach retries. Customers see 504s and lots of frontend retries.

chris.sre: can you paste the sample traces/logs? is this scale-up lag or auth flakiness?

maya.dev: attaching snippets from the attach-service and warmup logs. pattern: many concurrent attach attempts, then immediate cancels, then reattach, repeat.
```
attach-service: attach_request id=abcd started pool=dedicated-prio
warmup: gpu_init start id=abcd
attach-service: attach_request id=efgh started pool=dedicated-prio
warmup: gpu_init failed id=abcd reason=preflight_timeout
attach-service: attach_cancel id=abcd
warmup: gpu_init start id=efgh
```

olivia.support: customers report retries → 504s and auth 401 spikes for a subset of calls during the window. We correlated with scale events. Incident created: INC-2456.

infra-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool=dedicated-prio queue_length=420 attach_fail_rate=18% p99_latency=4.9s (5m)

oncall: noticed a lot of concurrent attach fanout to same node images. could be thundering herd on kernel image pulls + node warmup.

felix.runtime: quick hypothesis: when many attaches hit, our pool provisioning decides to spin new nodes but image pull / cuda init takes ~30-60s; meanwhile clients retry with exponential base that's too aggressive and restart attach loop. Need to confirm if backoff jitter is active for this queue.

jack.eng: repro steps i used in staging: ramped n=200 concurrent attach to reserved pool with small min_pool (0) and observed attach funnel / requeue. Commands i ran: 
```
# simulate attach flood
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT/attach -d '{"pool":"dedicated-prio"}' &
done
```

chris.sre: ok. immediate mitigations i can push: 1) increase min_prewarm for dedicated-prio to 2 for next 30m, 2) add jittered backoff to attach retry (client-side) via a temporary header-based override, 3) reduce attach fanout to 4 per request in the routing policy. any objections?

tara.pm: we should also plan a short customer-safe fallback: route AkmeCorp traffic to their hosted-verified model variant while we stabilize, to avoid invoice/UX risk. They approved fallback if we trigger it.

maya.dev: go for the mitigations. chris — please also capture metric deltas and post here. felix — can you validate kernel/image cache counts on pool nodes?

felix.runtime: looking now. initial readout: many nodes had image_pull_count spikes and dockerd churn. cache hit ratio for kernel image on warmup nodes ~42% (should be >95%). Kernel cache TTL on prewarm agents looks mis-set; see agent config snapshot.

olivia.support: pushing customer notice: "we're aware and applying a temporary routing fix to avoid delays during your billing window, ETA 10m" :hourglass_flowing_sand:

chris.sre: applied min_prewarm=2 and reduced attach_fanout to 4 for dedicated-prio. also enabled header override header: X-Attach-Backoff=exponential-jitter-2000ms. watching metrics.

infra-bot: [info] config-change: min_prewarm(dedicated-prio)=2 by chris.sre at 2456789100

oncall: p99 dropped to ~1.7s after changes (5m window) — still higher than baseline but improving. attach_fail_rate -> 6%.

maya.dev: good. action items: 
- felix: fix kernel image cache TTL on prewarm agents (PR + deploy)
- chris: formalize temporary header override and add a 1h automated rollback if error rate falls below threshold
- jack: create a small loadtest to validate the backoff under different fanouts
- olivia: update AkmeCorp once fallback complete and confirm they can accept hosted fallback if needed

jack.eng: i'll run the staging loadtest now and post results.

felix.runtime: created PR to set cache TTL to 24h and increase prefetch concurrency for prewarm worker. link: https://git.redwood/pr/998 — will roll to canary in 15m.

olivia.support: customer confirms temporary routing accepted. putting incident on watch. :white_check_mark:

chris.sre: keeping this thread open. if p99 stays >2s after PR roll and warming, escalate to infra for node image pre-populate.

maya.dev: thanks team. summary for incident log: dedicated-prio experienced throttled warmups due to thundering attach fanout + low image cache hit rate → caused p99 regressions and client retry storms; mitigated by increasing min_prewarm, reducing attach fanout, applying jittered backoff, and routing customer to hosted variant as fallback.

oncall: note: we should add a small monitoring alarm for kernel_image_cache_hit_ratio < 80% for priority pools.

chris.sre: created follow-up ticket INFRA-622: "prewarm kernel image caching & attach backoff defaults" and assigned to felix + jack.

maya.dev: closing loop here, will keep an eye during next billing window. :eyes:
